summary: Today’s pulse tracks Andy Burnham announces new homes scheme for first-time buyers, Trump rejects Iran deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days, and Ranulph Fiennes’ stepson appeals for funds to ‘locate and safeguard’ the explorer. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are people, first, and buyers. In the background, US strikes on Ecuadorian fishing boats raise humanitarian concerns but Trump admin not wavering and Pope Leo celebrates open-air mass before 700,000 people in Paris keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Andy Burnham announces new homes scheme for first-time buyers
headlines.description: Exclusive: Policy initiative for England will help more young people on to property ladder, prime minister tells Guardian A new help-to-buy scheme aimed at giving first-time buyers who cannot rely on the “bank of mum and dad” is to be introduced in a big policy announcement by Andy Burnham. The programme, called “Your first home”, is intended to help buyers in England who have a regular income but have been unable to save for a large deposit or don’t have financial support from their family.

headlines.title: Trump rejects Iran deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days
headlines.description: The US president says Tehran had only put forward the proposal because it is losing the war.

headlines.title: Ranulph Fiennes’ stepson appeals for funds to ‘locate and safeguard’ the explorer
headlines.description: Alexander Millington-Cotes is concerned for welfare of the 82-year-old, who hasn’t been seen in public for two years The stepson of Sir Ranulph Fiennes has launched a crowdfunder to pay for “specialist legal advice” in an attempt to locate the explorer, who hasn’t been seen in public for more than two years. Alexander Millington-Cotes, 31, has set a target of £55,000 for the fundraiser, to enable him to instruct lawyers to “locate and safeguard” Fiennes.

headlines.title: US strikes on Ecuadorian fishing boats raise humanitarian concerns but Trump admin not wavering
headlines.description: Attorney says fishers ‘losing their livelihoods’, but Marco Rubio maintains US still willing to ‘blow up ships if need be’ While the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio , was being decorated in Quito by Ecuador’s president for “helping to promote peace in the region”, 10 Ecuadorian fishers whose boat had been blown up by US forces were adrift in the eastern Pacific. On 8 September, a day before Rubio arrived, a US patrol vessel intercepted the fishing boat Don Rufo in international waters near Ecuador.

headlines.title: Pope Leo celebrates open-air mass before 700,000 people in Paris
headlines.description: Crowds line Place de la Concorde on second day of pontiff’s first official papal visit to France in 18 years Hundreds of thousands of people lined the Avenue des Champs-Élysées in ⁠Paris on Saturday to attend an open-air mass with Pope Leo, on the second day of his visit to France. The Vatican estimated 700,000 people turned out for the outdoor mass with the 71-year-old American pope – about 100,000 more than the number of people who had registered to attend.

headlines.title: German town bans 'stumbling stone' memorials to Nazi victims
headlines.description: Germany's education minister has branded the ban on the small brass memorial plaques a "scandal".

headlinePool.title: Watch: Bangkok declared flood disaster zone
headlinePool.description: Heavy rain over the last two days has overwhelmed Bangkok's water systems, with more rain forecast on Sunday.

headlinePool.title: California man charged in the killing of his ex-wife – two decades after she vanished
headlinePool.description: Authorities discovered a body hidden in a home’s crawlspace in 2020, 13 years after Jill Maiorca disappeared A man was recently charged in California with the killing of his ex-wife six years after her remains were discovered in a crawlspace beneath a home – and about two decades after when she went missing, according to investigators. Jeff Maiorca, 53, faces a charge of murder in the death of Jill Maiorca, who was 29 when she was killed, authorities said in discussing what could be one of the latest cases in the US to be solved with modern DNA techniques.

headlinePool.title: Jill Dando murder: technological advances allow police to review CCTV 27 years later
headlinePool.description: BBC broadcaster was shot in 1999 in case detectives have previously said may never be solved Technological advances are allowing police to review old CCTV footage in the unsolved murder of the BBC broadcaster Jill Dando, Scotland Yard has revealed. Advances in CCTV enhancement technology have allowed detectives to return to 27-year-old footage of Putney Bridge Underground station, Scotland Yard said. But detectives stressed that the review was part of existing inquiries – not a new investigation.

headlinePool.title: Security lapses at Utah campus where Charlie Kirk was killed, review says
headlinePool.description: The indpendent report also says Kirk's aides insisted he speak outdoors, overriding concerns from campus officials.

headlinePool.title: Pennsylvania measles outbreak spreads, with 55 new cases reported since Wednesday
headlinePool.description: 173 people hospitalized and four deaths in state so far, with less than 1% of those infected having been vaccinated The Pennsylvania department of health (DOH) announced on Friday that 55 new measles cases had been reported in the state since Wednesday, with officials continuing efforts to contain an outbreak of the disease that has spread across dozens of counties. In a news release , the DOH said that 890 measles cases had been confirmed across 39 counties in the state so far for the year. The outbreak had resulted in 173 hospitalizations in the state and four measles-associated deaths , the statement added.

headlinePool.title: Power outages and flooded roads as major storm bears down on US north-east
headlinePool.description: Thousands already without without power as New Jersey, Massachusetts, Delaware and New York brace for nor’easter More than 70,000 customers were without electricity in the north-eastern US on Saturday, a major sign of a powerful storm known as a nor’easter that was expected to create dangerous conditions through the weekend. Forecasters warned of gale winds that could down trees and heavy inundations that could flood roads.

headlinePool.title: Huge crowds greet Pope in Paris for open-air Mass
headlinePool.description: More than half a million people are expected to attend the event in the heart of the French capital.

headlinePool.title: New research finds 485 chemicals in US pesticide products linked to breast cancer
headlinePool.description: Paper raises questions about safety of food and other products as early onset breast cancer rates surge worldwide New research has identified at least 485 chemicals used in US pesticide products that are linked to breast cancer, raising questions about the safety of food and other products at a time when early onset breast cancer rates are surging worldwide . The new peer-reviewed paper , published in Environmental Health Perspectives, a top journal from the American Chemical Society, highlights what public health advocates say are a range of deficiencies in how US pesticides are regulated. The review includes active pesticide ingredients, but also hundreds of so-called “inert”, or inactive, ingredients that typically do not undergo a thorough safety review.
